title: Data Formats, Serialization and Data Integration
name: 6. Data Formats, Serialization and Data Integration
description: Master row vs columnar storage architectures, CSV, JSON, XML, Apache Avro, Apache Parquet, Apache ORC, in-memory Apache Arrow, Protocol Buffers, MessagePack, data compression (Snappy, GZIP, Zstandard, LZ4), schema definition and evolution, Confluent Schema Registry, REST API ingestion with cursor pagination, exponential backoff with jitter, HMAC webhook verification, and robust data contracts.

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between data serialization and deserialization?
options: Serialization encrypts data; deserialization decrypts data
Serialization converts memory data structures into transferable bytes/text; deserialization reconstructs memory objects from bytes/text
Serialization compresses data with GZIP; deserialization extracts it
Serialization is only used in SQL databases
quiz.explanation: Serialization translates an in-memory data object into a stream of bytes or text for storage/network transmission; deserialization reverses the process.

quiz.question: Why is Parquet or ORC preferred over CSV for analytical queries scanning millions of rows?
options: CSV files cannot be opened in Python
Parquet stores data column by column, allowing query engines to read only the required columns and skip row groups via statistics
CSV files are always encrypted
Parquet does not support numbers
quiz.explanation: Columnar formats like Parquet allow selective column reading (projection pushdown) and row-group skipping (predicate pushdown), drastically reducing I/O.

quiz.question: What is the key advantage of JSON Lines (JSONL / NDJSON) over standard JSON arrays for streaming data pipelines?
options: JSON Lines does not require quotes around strings
Each line is an independent JSON object, allowing incremental streaming and appending without loading the whole file into RAM
JSON Lines is a binary protocol
JSON Lines replaces SQL entirely
quiz.explanation: Standard JSON arrays require parsing the entire closing bracket, whereas JSON Lines allows line-by-line streaming, appending, and crash recovery.

quiz.question: In Apache Avro binary serialization, why is the resulting message payload significantly smaller than JSON?
options: Avro replaces text with random numbers
Avro binary encoding omits field names from every record, relying instead on an external schema for decoding
Avro only supports integers up to 255
Avro deletes null values permanently
quiz.explanation: Unlike JSON which repeats keys in every record ('customer_id': 101, 'name': 'Rahul'), Avro serializes only values into compact binary according to the schema.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of Apache Arrow in modern data engineering architectures?
options: A persistent disk file format to replace Parquet
A standardized in-memory columnar memory format enabling zero-copy data sharing between Python, Spark, and DuckDB
A message queue to replace Apache Kafka
An API gateway for microservices
quiz.explanation: Arrow standardizes in-memory columnar layout so systems (like Pandas, Polars, DuckDB, Spark) can exchange datasets without serialization overhead.
